title: The Durranis and the Singhs Exchange Formal Challenges

blocks.text: This page is built around taunt and answer. The Pathans try to define the Singhs as cowards who flee at mere arrival, while the Khalsa responds by stating its own terms for honorable combat rather than accepting the enemy's theatrical advantage.

The Sikh reply narrows the issue with striking confidence: they will fight only when they are armed with their small firearms, because the form of combat must match the discipline and practice that the Guru has sanctioned for them. Public negotiation thus becomes another way of asserting Panthic self-definition.
The atmosphere tightens toward a single-combat trial. Beneath the boasting, both sides understand that the moral prestige of the encounter may matter as much as the immediate tactical result.
